ModMetaData.name: Celestial Lighting
ModMetaData.author: Joof
ModMetaData.description:
Sunlight, moonlight and weather, rebuilt around a real solar model: the sun's actual position for your colony's latitude, season and time of day.
Celestial Lighting simulates the sun, moon and planet to get beautiful visuals without affecting gameplay.
## Sun and Shadows
- Seasonal sun positoning that changes angle of the shadows - Sunrise and sunset simulate twilight and can be seen in the north / south lattitudes. - More dynamic shadow casting.
## Night and Moon
- Night brightness from starlight, airglow and moonlight. - The moon simulates a full lunar cycle and casts its own shadows. - Darker nights controllable with a slider. - Darker interiors controllable with a slider. - Colour drains toward blue-grey in low light - the Purkinje shift -
## Sky and Weather - Rain, snow, fog and cloud dim the sky, per weather. Many modded weathers are supported. - Clouds you can see - sheets of cloud drift over the map, more of them the cloudier it is, and they take their colour from the light on them. Can be switched off. - Sky colour temperature shifts warm and cool with the sun's altitude. - Auroras you can actually see, during solar flares and vanilla aurora events - and never otherwise. - Eclipses events are modeled more realistically. - Blood-moon nights turn crimson if Vanilla Races Expanded - Sanguophage is installed.
## Settings and Presets
Every effect has its own on/off switch. Available pre-sets:
- Cinematic (default) - Less physics-bound. Brighter nights and interiors. - Realistic - Emulates the real-world more closely. Interiors are pitch-black and nights are dark by default.
## FAQ
Q. Does this change gameplay?
No default setting does and never will.
Optional settings may have some impact: - Natural eclipses. Simulated eclipses that occur when the moon passes the sun. - Realistic day length. Makes days their real-world lengths as opposed to vanilla. This allows for polar summers and winters.
Q. Are the darker nights are purely cosmetic?
Yes, the game lighting values remain the same.
Q. Can I add or remove it mid-save?
Yes, both. Nothing this mod makes is written into your save - no items, buildings or world state - so removing it leaves the colony exactly as it was. Loading a save that once had it installed may print a few red errors on that first load only; they are harmless.
Q. Does it work with Dub's Skylights?
Yes. Skylit rooms read the lighting this mod computes, through the same value Skylights already reads.
Q. Known conflicts?
Perspective: Eaves - Celestial Lighting re-implements the functionality in a compatible way. Tilt the Planet! - Incompatible. It renders the same sun, shadows and sky from its own tilt model, so the two fight over every frame. The inspiration for this mod - run one or the other.
Realistic Axial Tilt is supported, not conflicting: it owns the planet's tilt and seasons, Celestial Lighting renders the sky from the geometry it publishes.
Q. Does it work with Planetsmith?
Yes, and it now follows it. Planetsmith lets you pick a planet's axial tilt when you generate a world, and Celestial Lighting lights that world on the tilt it was actually generated with - so a steeply tilted planet gets a sun that climbs higher in summer and stays lower in winter, with the shadows to match, and an upright one gets a sun that barely moves all year. The sky agrees with the biomes instead of ignoring them.
Day length is not affected, because Planetsmith does not set one - it decides which biomes go where, not how long the day is. If you want the long polar summers and dark winters a steep tilt implies, turn on "Realistic day length" as well.
There is no switch for this and that is deliberate: the tilt is Planetsmith's setting, so change it in Planetsmith. A second control here would only let the sky and the biomes disagree again, which is the whole thing this fixes. The settings screen shows you which mod is setting the tilt and what it is. The same is true of Realistic Axial Tilt, which has always owned the tilt outright.
Q. Does it work with Realistic Planets 2?
Yes, and it follows that one too. Realistic Planets 2 lets you pick an axial tilt when you generate a world, and Celestial Lighting lights the world on it, exactly as it does for Planetsmith. An earlier release of Realistic Planets 2 had a sky engine of its own and the two would have fought; the current one has removed it, so there is nothing left to collide with.
One difference worth knowing. Realistic Planets 2 also has its own calendar, and it runs about 15 days ahead of RimWorld's - so on one of its worlds your longest day arrives a fortnight before your warmest one. Celestial Lighting follows the planet rather than the calendar, so the sun is where Realistic Planets 2 says it is. That is its year, not a fault in the sky.
As with Planetsmith, there is no switch: the tilt is Realistic Planets 2's setting, and the settings screen reports which mod is setting it and what it is.
Q. Does it work with Biomes! Caverns?
Yes. An underground map has no sky, so sunrise and sunset colour, sky colour temperature, moonlight, auroras, blood moons and eclipses all switch themselves off down there, and shadows follow the biome's own "no shadows" setting.
Caves do render dark, because a sealed cave has no sky to light it - that is the intended result rather than a conflict, and lamps and torches work normally. If you prefer Caverns' brighter ambient-lit look, raise "Minimum indoor brightness" or turn off "Black unlit interiors".
Q. Can I use pieces of this mod in my work?
Absolutely — it's MIT licensed, so take whatever's useful, no permission needed. https://github.com/Jeffrharr/CelestialLighting
Q. Did you use AI to create any part of this mod?
I used LLMs to write the code and the thumbnail. I'm a software engineer, but not an artist.
Requires Harmony.
